newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Golden Crescent drug trade at $5bln - U.N. report.
newsitem.headline: Golden Crescent drug trade at $5bln - U.N. report.

text.p: A U.N. drugs control body said on Thursday illicit drug business in the so-called Golden Crescent of Iran, Afghanistan and Pakistan was estimated at $5 billion per year in a global drug trade of $400 billion.

"Big money is certainly not made in this part of the world," United Nations International Drug Control Programme (UNDCP) director Giovanni Quaglia told a news conference at the launch of the first World Drug Report prepared by the UNDCP.
"When we take the illicit market, or size of business of all these drugs, it has been estimated around $400 billion per year," Quaglia said.

"When we look at the region -- it is very difficult to separate what is going on in Pakistan or Afghanistan or Iran, the things are quite intrinsically linked -- we do estimate that the volume of the drug trade is about $5 billion."
The report said 90 percent of the world's illicitly produced opiates originated in the two main production areas - the Golden Crescent and the Golden Triangle (Laos, Burma, Thailand).
He said a kg (2.2 lbs)of heroin was worth $3,000 in Pakistan's industrial port city of Karachi compared with a street value of more than $50,000 in the United States.

Pakistan is estimated to have produced about 120 tonnes of opium in the 1994/95 crop year, while output in Afghanistan, one of world's top opiate producers, was estimated between 2,200 and 2,400 tonnes.

Quaglia said UNDCP had launched a $16 million four-year programme in June to discourage poppy cultivation in the Afghan provinces of Kandahar and Nangahar with the help of the Islamic Taleban militia.
"It is precisely to test the willingness and the capacity of the Taleban to get rid of opium in the target areas with the assistance of international community," he said.

"We are working mainly with the Taleban, because 90 to 95 percent of the area under poppy cultivation is under Taleban control," he said but added that this did not mean that Taleban was linked with drugs.
